tasks.short: Work out how to diagnose and repair a vehicle using fault codes, manuals, charts and experience.

steps.what: Technician reads the work order and the customer's complaint
Technician runs the diagnostic tester and reads fault codes and live data
Technician looks up repair procedures, wiring charts and torque values in technical manuals

loop.input: Fault codes, vehicle identification and complaint text, plus the workshop's closed work orders with cause and correction, and the manufacturer's service bulletins.
loop.output: Up to three likely causes, each with links to the matching repair procedure and the past work orders or bulletins behind it.
loop.check: Every procedure link must exist for this vehicle's model and engine code; every cause must cite at least one past work order or bulletin ID that shares a fault code; nothing is shown when no citation matches.
loop.stop: One search per work order; three suggestions at most; the technician decides.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fault-code lookup gives generic procedures; the workshop's past fixes are free text that only a reading step can match.

steps.what: Technician plans work procedures: repair approach and order of steps from experience
Technician asks the workshop foreman or manufacturer helpdesk about hard cases
Workshop foreman or helpdesk advises on the difficult repair
Technician notes planned steps, labour time and parts on the work order

tasks.design: The diagnostic tester's fault codes and the vehicle identification on the work order in the workshop system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) open the matching procedures in the manufacturer's service portal on the {PARTNER_PORTAL}. A bounded model step searches the workshop's own closed work orders and service bulletins for likely causes, each tied to a cited record, and the chosen procedure fills labour time and parts on the work order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Past fixes lived in technicians' heads and free-text work orders, and manuals were searched page by page.
tasks.enabler_now: Manufacturers publish service information online, workshop systems hold years of closed work orders, and language models can match free-text fixes when a check ties each answer to a record.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults and unusual damage need hands-on testing; past work orders are only useful if cause and correction were written down.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing, feeling and testing a fault, and knowing when the book is wrong for this car.

ambition.what: Every repeat repair checked against earlier fixes on the same model, so comebacks are caught before the car leaves.

tasks.altitude: The technician spends less time searching and more on diagnosis; decisions on the repair stay theirs.

reach.learn: Whether fleet repair history gives better suggestions than dealer history.

evidence.claim: Manufacturers' online service portals give repair procedures, wiring diagrams and torque values per vehicle.
Vehicle manufacturers must give independent workshops access to repair and maintenance information under EU type-approval rules.
If work order time stamps are used to watch technician speed, the works council must consent first.
Using workshop logs to evaluate staff performance would bring the AI step into a high-risk area; it is used here only to suggest causes.

assumptions: Boundary: from reading the work order to the planned repair on the work order; customer approval of the quote and the repair itself are outside.

Input contract: closed work orders with fault codes, cause and correction fields, written by technicians in the workshop system; vehicle identification on the work order from the service advisor; manufacturer bulletins from the service portal; fallback is manual searching.
Technicians fill cause and correction for each closed job; that upkeep is counted.
Foreman and helpdesk time is outside the technician's savings.
unknowns: How many years of work orders hold usable cause and correction text.
Whether the manufacturer portal allows deep links from fault codes.
research_questions: How often does the first suggested cause turn out to be the fix?

already_counted.description: Technician checks suggested causes and procedure links against the vehicle.

incremental.description: Technician writes cause and correction on every closed work order.
Workshop IT maintains the search index, portal links and model costs.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Workshops with thin work order history get few cited suggestions, so savings come only from faster manual links.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technician keeps diagnosis, judgement and the repair; searching manuals and writing up plans shrink.
reach: Bus and truck mechanics' fleet repairs
Service advisors' quotes from planned work orders
skills_to_grow: Writing clear cause and correction notes
Judging suggested causes against the vehicle in front of them
role.ambitious_version: A technician whose own repair notes make the whole workshop faster at the next similar fault.
